notes: Asks about grid mutation and diagonal adjacency before writing anything. Chooses BFS with a visited set specifically to avoid mutating the caller's grid, and says why. Correct on the first submission. States complexity in terms of both grid dimensions rather than a vague 'linear'.

turns.text: So I'm counting connected components of '1' cells in a character grid.
Two questions before I start: is adjacency four-directional or does diagonal count, and am I allowed to mutate the input grid?

Four-directional, and I'd rather not mutate the input even if I'm allowed to — a scoring function that destroys its argument is a nasty surprise for the caller. I'll keep a visited set instead. BFS from each unvisited land cell. That's my plan — I'm ready to start coding.
All green, including the all-water and single-cell grids. I'm done here, happy to move on.

Time is O(m * n) — every cell is enqueued at most once because I mark it visited at enqueue time, not at dequeue time. Space is O(m * n) too, for the visited set plus the queue in the worst case where the whole grid is one island.
